paper_title: First indirect detection constraints on axions in the Solar basin
notes: Paper (DeRocco et al., arXiv:2205.05700) sets first indirect-detection limits on keV-mass axions in the Solar basin using NuSTAR quiescent solar observations. Primary result relevant here is Fig. 2: 90% CL limits on g_agamma (with g_aee=0) for m = 3-40 keV, world-leading for 5-30 keV, improving on horizontal branch star cooling (g_agamma ~ 6.6e-11 GeV^-1) by over an order of magnitude. No numerical table is provided; data_points are approximate values read from the described Fig. 2 CLs/Yellin exclusion curve, anchored by the stated >10x improvement over the HB bound in the 5-30 keV range and the plot's y-axis range (1e-12 to 1e-9 GeV^-1). CLs limit weakens below ~8 keV due to the 4 keV energy cutoff. This is a solar-basin (bound axion) search, not a local DM halo search, so no local DM density is assumed. Paper also constrains g_aee and the f_a (universal coupling) plane; AxionPhoton (Fig. 2) chosen as the primary standalone coupling result. | [VISION GATE D] vision notes admit tracing a compilation envelope ('union of') rather than the paper's own single curve | selector: text over figure_vision (quality (1, 1, 1, 1, 3, 0, 0.55, 7))
